products_in_scope_notes: ZenChat is evaluating Redwood Hosted API for chat + embeddings for their support-agent product; procurement is pushing for Dedicated capacity as a Phase 2 option if spend ramps. They want predictability and a contractually tight definition of what is billable usage to avoid invoice disputes.
requirements_summary: Workload: high-volume chat completions with streaming + tool/function calls; embeddings for doc search (batch). Targets: p95 < 900ms time-to-first-token for EU users; predictable cost per resolved ticket. Routing: wants fallback to a second model/region during capacity events but requires clear billing attribution. Observability: needs daily usage export aligned to their billing timezone; wants billed vs raw tokens shown to Finance. Compliance: EU data residency preference; retention controls for request logs; audit logging of metering/billing access.
discount_and_credits_status: Requested: (1) 15% discount on usage rates for first 12 months, (2) one-time $25k service credits to offset migration + eval period, (3) cap on overage rate increases for renewal. Current status (as of 2026-02-26): under Finance/Legal review; Redwood position is discount contingent on 12-month minimum commit and explicit contract language that credits apply only to token-based charges (no cash refund), expire in 6 months, and do not apply retroactively. Awaiting CFO sign-off on final numbers and guardrails.
legal_redlines_summary: ZenChat counsel redlined the Usage Definition and Billing section with focus on: (a) token definition (prompt vs completion; tool-call tokens; structured outputs), (b) retries/timeouts/fallback routing (ensure no double-billing), (c) streaming semantics (partial chunks / client disconnect), (d) caching (whether cache hits are billed; require invoice visibility), (e) dispute window (requested 90 days vs Redwood standard), (f) audit rights for metering logic + access logs, (g) data retention/residency commitments tied to usage logs.
proposed_usage_definition_language_worki: Working agreement direction from 2026-02-11 call: define billable usage as 'billed_tokens' as reported by Redwood Usage API/export for the applicable model endpoint; explicitly exclude server-side retries from double-counting (idempotency/dedupe at the usage-event level). For caching: Redwood to surface cache_hit attribution fields; ZenChat requesting that cache-hit responses are either (i) billed at $0 token charge or (ii) billed at a discounted rate, but in either case must be transparent in exports/invoice line items. Streaming: bill only tokens successfully generated by the model up to termination; clarify behavior for client disconnect vs server abort. Open item: whether request-count is a billable meter (Redwood: no separate per-request fee today; used for rate limits and operational analytics).
